What is the name of NaCl?\nsodium chlori:
1) NaCl is a metal with a nonmetal, so it is ionic.
2) Name the metal first, then the nonmetal with the ending -ide.
Answer: sodium chloride.
Why the others are wrong: chlorine is the element name and chlorate is a polyatomic ion with oxygen.
What is the name of MgO?\nmagnesium oxid:
1) MgO is ionic (metal plus nonmetal).
2) Name Mg as magnesium and change oxygen to oxide.
Answer: magnesium oxide.
Why the others are wrong: ionic names use -ide, not the element name, and never use prefixes.
Which prefix means three in the name of:
1) The prefixes in order are mono 1, di 2, tri 3, tetra 4, penta 5.
2) Three corresponds to tri.
Answer: tri.
Why the others are wrong: tetra is 4 and di is 2.
What is the correct name of CO2?\ncarbon:
1) Both elements are nonmetals, so use prefixes.
2) One C needs no mono, and two O is di with ending -ide.
Answer: carbon dioxide.
Why the others are wrong: carbon monoxide is CO, and mono is not used on the first element.
What is the correct name of FeCl3?\niron:
1) Three Cl- give a total charge of -3.
2) One Fe must be 3+, so the name needs the Roman numeral III.
Answer: iron(III) chloride.
Why the others are wrong: iron(II) chloride is FeCl2, and prefixes are not used for ionic compounds.
What is the correct name of CuSO4?\ncopp:
1) SO4 is the polyatomic ion sulfate with charge 2-.
2) One Cu balances it, so Cu is 2+.
3) Name: copper(II) sulfate.
Answer: copper(II) sulfate.
Why the others are wrong: sulfide is S 2- and sulfite is SO3 2-.
What is the correct name of N2O5?\ndinit:
1) Both elements are nonmetals, so use prefixes.
2) Two N is dinitrogen and five O is pentoxide (the a of penta is dropped).
Answer: dinitrogen pentoxide.
Why the others are wrong: the first element needs di because there are two atoms, and dinitrogen oxide is N2O.
What is the correct name of Ca(OH)2?\nca:
1) OH is the polyatomic ion hydroxide.
2) Ca is a metal, so the compound is ionic and takes no prefixes.
Answer: calcium hydroxide.
Why the others are wrong: the ion keeps its single name, and prefixes are not used for ionic compounds.
What is the correct name of Fe2O3?\niron:
1) Three O 2- give a charge of 3 x (-2) = -6.
2) Two Fe must total +6, so each Fe is 3+.
3) Name: iron(III) oxide.
Answer: iron(III) oxide.
Why the others are wrong: the Roman numeral is the charge of one ion, not the subscript, so II and VI do not fit.
What is the correct name of (NH4)2S?\nam:
1) NH4+ is the ammonium ion and S 2- is sulfide.
2) Name the cation first, then the anion.
Answer: ammonium sulfide.
Why the others are wrong: sulfite is SO3 2-, and ammonia is the neutral molecule NH3.
What is the formula of sodium chloride?\:
1) Sodium forms Na+ and chlorine forms Cl-.
2) One of each balances the charge.
Answer: NaCl.
Why the others are wrong: extra subscripts would make the charges unbalanced or are not reduced.
What is the charge of the calcium ion?\n:
1) Calcium is in Group 2 and has two valence electrons.
2) It loses both to form a cation.
Answer: 2+.
Why the others are wrong: a metal loses electrons, so its charge is positive, and Group 1 gives 1+.
What is the formula of carbon monoxide?\:
1) Mono means one oxygen.
2) The first element has no prefix, so one carbon.
Answer: CO.
Why the others are wrong: CO2 is carbon dioxide with two oxygen atoms.
What is the formula of magnesium chlorid:
1) Ions are Mg 2+ and Cl-.
2) Criss-cross the charge numbers to get Mg1Cl2.
3) Drop the 1.
Answer: MgCl2.
Why the others are wrong: MgCl would leave a net charge of +1.
What is the formula of aluminum oxide?\n:
1) Ions are Al 3+ and O 2-.
2) Criss-cross: Al gets 2 and O gets 3.
3) Check 2(+3) + 3(-2) = 0.
Answer: Al2O3.
Why the others are wrong: Al3O2 has the numbers criss-crossed the wrong way.
What is the formula of calcium hydroxide:
1) Ions are Ca 2+ and OH-.
2) Two OH- are needed, so put OH in parentheses with a subscript 2.
Answer: Ca(OH)2.
Why the others are wrong: CaOH2 would mean only the H is doubled.
What is the formula of iron(II) sulfate?:
1) Iron(II) is Fe 2+ and sulfate is SO4 2-.
2) One of each gives a total charge of zero.
Answer: FeSO4.
Why the others are wrong: Fe2(SO4)3 is iron(III) sulfate.
What is the formula of diphosphorus pent:
1) Di means two phosphorus atoms.
2) Penta means five oxygen atoms.
Answer: P2O5.
Why the others are wrong: P5O2 swaps the numbers, and P2O3 has only three oxygen atoms.
What is the formula of aluminum sulfate?:
1) Ions are Al 3+ and SO4 2-.
2) Criss-cross: Al gets 2 and SO4 gets 3, written in parentheses.
3) Check 2(+3) + 3(-2) = 0.
Answer: Al2(SO4)3.
Why the others are wrong: Al3(SO4)2 gives +9 and -4.
How many atoms are in one formula unit o:
1) Ca: 3 atoms.
2) P: 2 atoms.
3) O: 2 x 4 = 8. Total 3 + 2 + 8 = 13.
Answer: 13.
Why the others are wrong: 9 forgets the subscript outside the parentheses on oxygen and 11 leaves out the phosphorus.
What does the law of conservation of mas:
1) Atoms are rearranged in a reaction, not created or destroyed.
2) So the total mass stays constant.
Answer: The total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.
Why the others are wrong: no mass is gained or lost in an ordinary chemical reaction.
In a chemical equation, what are the sub:
1) The arrow means yields.
2) Substances that start the reaction are on the left.
Answer: reactants.
Why the others are wrong: products are on the right of the arrow.
What does the symbol (aq) mean in a chem:
1) State symbols are (s), (l), (g) and (aq).
2) aq comes from aqueous.
Answer: dissolved in water.
Why the others are wrong: (g) means gas and (s) means solid.
When balancing a chemical equation, whic:
1) A subscript is part of the identity of a substance.
2) Only coefficients may be changed to balance atoms.
Answer: changing coefficients in front of formulas.
Why the others are wrong: changing a subscript turns H2O into a different substance.
What are the balanced coefficients, in o:
1) N: 2 atoms on the left needs 2 NH3.
2) Then H on the right is 6, so 3 H2.
3) N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3.
Answer: 1, 3, 2.
Why the others are wrong: 1, 3, 1 leaves N unbalanced.
How many oxygen atoms are in 2Al2(SO4)3?:
1) One Al2(SO4)3 has 3 sulfate ions with 4 O each, so 12 O.
2) Multiply by the coefficient 2: 24.
Answer: 24.
Why the others are wrong: 12 forgets the coefficient 2.
In the reaction 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, 4.0 g:
1) By conservation of mass, the product mass equals the reactant mass.
2) 4.0 + 32.0 = 36.0 g.
Answer: 36.0 g.
Why the others are wrong: subtracting the masses (28.0 g) ignores that all the mass is conserved.
What is the sum of the coefficients when:
1) Balance C: 3 CO2.
2) Balance H: 4 H2O.
3) O on the right is 6 + 4 = 10, so 5 O2. Sum: 1 + 5 + 3 + 4 = 13.
Answer: 13.
Why the others are wrong: 12 forgets the coefficient 1 in front of C3H8.

1) Ca: 3 Ca(OH)2 gives 3 Ca.
2) P: 2 H3PO4 gives 2 P.
3) H on the left is 6 + 6 = 12, so 6 H2O. Equation: 3, 2, 1, 6. Sum = 12.
Answer: 12.
Why the others are wrong: 3 Ca(OH)2 + 2 H3PO4 is required, not a 1 : 1 ratio.
The balanced equation is 4Fe + 3O2 -> 2F:
1) The mole ratio Fe to O2 is 4 : 3.
2) mol O2 = 8 x 3/4 = 6.
Answer: 6 mol.
Why the others are wrong: 12 mol comes from inverting the ratio (8 x 3/2 is not 4 : 3).
What type of reaction is A + B -> AB?\ns:
1) Two reactants combine.
2) One product forms.
Answer: synthesis.
Why the others are wrong: decomposition goes the other way, from one reactant to several products.
What type of reaction is AB -> A + B?\nd:
1) There is one reactant.
2) It breaks into simpler products.
Answer: decomposition.
Why the others are wrong: synthesis has one product, not one reactant.
Which reaction type is a hydrocarbon rea:
1) The reactants are a hydrocarbon and O2.
2) Products CO2 and H2O with heat and light show burning.
Answer: combustion.
Why the others are wrong: synthesis would form only one product.
What type of reaction is 2Na + Cl2 -> 2N:
1) Two elements are the reactants.
2) They form a single compound.
Answer: synthesis.
Why the others are wrong: no element replaces another in a compound.
What type of reaction is Zn + 2HCl -> Zn:
1) One element (Zn) and one compound (HCl) react.
2) Zn replaces H in the compound.
Answer: single replacement.
Why the others are wrong: double replacement needs two compounds as reactants.
What type of reaction is AgNO3 + NaCl ->:
1) Two compounds are the reactants.
2) The partners swap: Ag pairs with Cl and Na pairs with NO3.
Answer: double replacement.
Why the others are wrong: single replacement needs a free element as a reactant.
What is a reaction between an acid and a:
1) Acid plus base swap ions.
2) The products are a salt and water, as in HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O.
Answer: neutralization.
Why the others are wrong: combustion needs oxygen reacting with a fuel.
What are the products of the complete co:
1) Complete combustion means plenty of oxygen.
2) Carbon becomes CO2 and hydrogen becomes H2O.
Answer: CO2 and H2O.
Why the others are wrong: CO forms only in incomplete combustion.
Which equation is a decomposition reacti:
1) A decomposition has one reactant and several products.
2) Only 2HgO -> 2Hg + O2 has a single reactant.
Answer: 2HgO -> 2Hg + O2.
Why the others are wrong: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O is a synthesis.
Which describes Pb(NO3)2(aq) + 2KI(aq) -:
1) Two aqueous compounds swap partners, so it is double replacement.
2) PbI2(s) is a solid forming in solution, a precipitate.
Answer: a double replacement that forms a precipitate.
Why the others are wrong: no gas forms and there is more than one reactant.
What does the activity series of metals:
1) The series lists metals from most to least reactive.
2) A higher metal replaces a lower one.
Answer: how easily metals react.
Why the others are wrong: density and melting point are physical properties not used to rank reactivity.
Which of these metals is the most reacti:
1) Potassium is near the top of the activity series.
2) Cu, Ag and Au are near the bottom.
Answer: potassium.
Why the others are wrong: copper, silver and gold are unreactive metals.
When does a single replacement reaction:
1) A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive one.
2) So the free metal must be higher in the series.
Answer: when the free metal is higher in the activity series than the metal in the compound.
Why the others are wrong: a lower metal cannot displace a higher one.
What are the products of Zn + CuSO4?\nZn:
1) Zn is above Cu in the series, so it replaces Cu.
2) Zn forms Zn 2+, giving ZnSO4.
3) Copper metal is released.
Answer: ZnSO4 and Cu.
Why the others are wrong: the reaction does occur, and zinc is 2+ so Zn2SO4 is wrong.
Which combination shows no reaction?\nCu:
1) Only metals above hydrogen replace H from an acid.
2) Cu is below hydrogen.
Answer: Cu + HCl.
Why the others are wrong: Mg, Zn and Fe are above hydrogen and release H2.
What are the products of Mg + 2HCl?\nMgC:
1) Mg is above hydrogen, so it reacts.
2) Mg 2+ with Cl- gives MgCl2.
3) Hydrogen is released as H2.
Answer: MgCl2 and H2.
Why the others are wrong: MgCl would have unbalanced charges.
Which precipitate forms when BaCl2(aq) a:
1) Swap partners: BaSO4 and NaCl.
2) Most sulfates are soluble except BaSO4, while NaCl is soluble.
Answer: BaSO4.
Why the others are wrong: NaCl stays dissolved.
Which is the balanced equation for Al +:
1) Al is above Cu, so Al replaces Cu and forms Al 3+, giving AlCl3.
2) Balance Cl: 6 on each side needs 2 AlCl3 and 3 CuCl2.
3) Then 2 Al and 3 Cu.
Answer: 2Al + 3CuCl2 -> 2AlCl3 + 3Cu.
Why the others are wrong: AlCl2 uses the wrong aluminum charge.
How many moles of CO2 form from the comp:
1) The mole ratio C3H8 to CO2 is 1 : 3.
2) 2 mol x 3 = 6 mol.
Answer: 6 mol.
Why the others are wrong: 3 mol is the amount from only 1 mol of C3H8.
What happens when aqueous KNO3 and aqueo:
1) Swap partners to get KCl and NaNO3.
2) Both are soluble, so there is no precipitate, gas or water.
3) The ions simply stay dissolved.
Answer: no reaction because all possible products are soluble.
Why the others are wrong: KCl and NaNO3 are both soluble salts.
